name: Brow growth serum
summary: Cosmetic serums sold to thicken brows; published evidence is limited to a safety test and one small unreported trial.
lead: Brow growth serums are cosmetic products marketed to make eyebrows look thicker or longer. Many are peptide- or botanical-based; Wikipedia notes that some lash-growth brands use peptides rather than prostaglandins because of regulations in Canada and California.

name: Vaseline on lashes/brows
summary: Dabbing petroleum jelly on lashes and brows as a cheap conditioner; no studies show it grows hair.
lead: Applying petroleum jelly (Vaseline is the best-known brand) to eyelashes and eyebrows is a grooming practice promoted as a way to condition hair and make lashes or brows look fuller or glossier. Petroleum jelly is a semi-solid hydrocarbon mixture widely used in skin products to reduce moisture loss.

name: Brow lift (surgical)
summary: Surgery that raises a drooping brow and opens the eye area; well-documented in the plastic surgery literature, popular in forum surgery packages.
lead: A surgical brow lift, also called a forehead lift, browlift or browplasty, is a cosmetic operation that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and softens horizontal forehead lines. It is also used when a heavy brow obstructs the upper visual field. Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, hairline (pretrichial), temporal, direct, mid-forehead and transblepharoplasty approaches.
claims: A higher or more lateral brow position improves facial attractiveness
Botulinum toxin can serve as a non-surgical brow lift
Bundling many procedures abroad is a practical route to a large change

name: Botox brow lift
summary: Small toxin injections that let the brow tails sit higher without surgery; temporary, with some trial data behind it.
lead: A botulinum toxin brow lift is a non-surgical technique in which small injections weaken muscles that pull the eyebrow down, letting the outer brow sit higher. Botox is the best-known brand; Dysport and others are also used.
claims: Botox can lift the brow tails without surgery

name: Don't over-pluck / regrow
summary: Stop plucking so brows can fill in; regrowth depends on whether follicles are intact, and no trials test it.
lead: "Don't over-pluck" is advice in looksmaxxing and grooming circles to stop tweezing eyebrows so that sparse areas can fill in. Tweezing is the most common way to shape brows, and Wikipedia notes that plucked hairs can stop growing back over time, though that statement is flagged as needing a citation.

name: Eyebrow gel with fibers
summary: Brow gel with tiny fibers that fake fullness; a temporary cosmetic with no clinical research.
lead: Eyebrow gel with fibers is a cosmetic that combines a brow-setting gel with tiny colored fibers that cling to hairs and skin to make brows look thicker or fill gaps. Wikipedia describes brow gels as adding texture and definition, and notes that powders, pencils and shaders are used to fill sparse areas; fibers specifically are not covered there.

name: Brow dyeing blonde / bleaching
summary: Lightening brows with peroxide bleach or dye as a style choice; common chemistry, no brow-specific research.
lead: Bleaching or dyeing the eyebrows lighter, often blonde, is a style practice used to soften or alter the look of the brow. Hair bleaching works by oxidizing melanin with hydrogen peroxide in an alkaline mixture, with home products typically around 6% peroxide and salon products up to 12%, according to Wikipedia.

name: Brow slitting / cuts
summary: A shaved gap cut through the eyebrow as a style statement; temporary, cosmetic, and barely studied.
lead: Brow slitting, also called eyebrow slits or brow cuts, is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines are shaved or cut through the eyebrow hair so that bare skin shows in a short vertical or diagonal gap. It is purely a hair-styling choice and is usually done with a razor or trimmer; it does not involve cutting skin.

name: Unibrow trimming / bridge shaping
summary: Removing or shaping the hair bridging the brows; cheap and reversible, with culture deciding whether it counts as a flaw.
lead: A unibrow, medically called synophrys, is hair that joins the two eyebrows across the glabella, the smooth area above the bridge of the nose. Unibrow trimming or bridge shaping is the grooming practice of removing or thinning that hair, by plucking, waxing, threading, shaving, or in some cases permanent hair-removal methods, so that the brows appear separate, or of deliberately keeping or shaping the bridge .

name: Eflornithine (Vaniqa)
summary: Prescription cream that slows facial hair regrowth in women; it works only while used and is not hair removal.
lead: Eflornithine, also known as difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), is an inhibitor of the enzyme ornithine decarboxylase. Its 13.9 percent topical cream, sold as Vaniqa, is a prescription product approved in the United States in December 2000 to reduce unwanted facial hair in women . Systemic forms of the same molecule are used for other conditions, including second-stage African sleeping sickness and, since 2023, maintenance therapy in high-risk neuroblastoma .

name: Electrolysis
summary: Needle-and-current destruction of individual follicles, the slow, per-hair route to FDA-recognised permanent removal on any hair colour.
lead: Electrolysis, in appearance contexts, is a hair-removal method in which a practitioner inserts a fine sterile probe into each hair follicle and applies electrical current to destroy the follicle's growth centre. It is used for the face, brows, hairline and body, and is distinct from the chemistry process of the same name .

name: Professional laser hair removal
summary: Clinic lasers that cut regrowth by roughly half or more over several sessions, best on dark hair and lighter skin.
lead: Professional laser hair removal is a clinic or medical-spa procedure in which pulses of laser or intense pulsed light heat the pigment in hair so that the follicle is damaged and regrowth is reduced. It is used on the face, neck, beard line, body and other areas, and is one of the most widely offered cosmetic hair-reduction treatments .

name: Hair-removal epilator
summary: Handheld device that yanks hairs out by the root; slower regrowth than shaving, but painful and not permanent.
lead: An epilator is an electric (or spring-powered) device that grips many hairs at once and pulls them out by the root as it passes over the skin. It works much like waxing but does not remove skin cells, and is used for legs, underarms, arms and, with small attachments, the face .

name: Body groomer (manscaping trimmer)
summary: An electric trimmer for shortening body hair rather than shaving it; little research exists beyond general clipper and shaving literature.
lead: A body groomer, often marketed as a manscaping trimmer, is an electric device with guarded blades intended to shorten or remove body hair on the chest, abdomen, underarms and other areas below the neck. It is a variant of the electric hair clipper and trimmer, which has been commercially available since the early 1920s.

name: Back shaver
summary: A long-handled razor or trimmer for reaching your own back; convenient by design, with no research specific to it.
lead: A back shaver is a razor or trimmer attached to an extended handle so that a person can remove or shorten hair on their own back and shoulders without help. It is a grooming tool within the broader category of body hair removal.

name: Bleaching body hair
summary: Chemically lightening dark body hair so it shows less; a cosmetic alternative to shaving with documented irritation risks and no male-specific research.
lead: Bleaching body hair is the practice of lightening dark body hair with an oxidizing cosmetic product so that it is less visible, as an alternative to removing it. Hair bleaching works by oxidation breaking down melanin, typically using hydrogen peroxide with persulfate salts and an alkaline agent.

name: Ingrown hair treatments (salicylic, tend skin)
summary: Salicylic-acid and similar after-shave products for razor bumps; the condition is well documented, branded products are not.
lead: Ingrown hair treatments are topical products, often containing salicylic acid, marketed to reduce bumps and irritation where shaved hairs curl back into the skin. Ingrown hairs, called pseudofolliculitis barbae in the beard area, are common after shaving, especially in people with tightly curled hair.

name: Aftershave balm / witch hazel
summary: Post-shave splash or balm, often containing witch hazel; widely used to soothe, with limited trial evidence.
lead: Aftershave is a product applied to the skin after shaving, traditionally an alcohol-based liquid called a splash and now also sold as balms, lotions and gels. Balms are usually alcohol-free and moisturizing, and witch hazel and bay rum are among the oldest aftershave ingredients.

name: Chest/body shaving for gym
summary: Shaving body hair to make muscle definition show; common among bodybuilders, with documented skin-infection risks in athletes.
lead: Chest and body shaving for the gym is the practice of removing body hair, mainly from the chest, abdomen and arms, so that muscle definition looks more visible. Wikipedia notes that bodybuilders and some other athletes shave body hair to highlight muscle development or reduce friction.

name: Full manscaping routine
summary: Head-to-toe male body-hair grooming, from trimming to full removal; widely practised, with risks that mirror whichever removal method is used.
lead: Manscaping is a portmanteau of 'man' and 'landscaping' that refers to trimming, shaping or removing male body hair. The earliest known use of the term is dated to 2003. A 'full manscaping routine' is an informal label for grooming several body regions in one regimen, typically chest, abdomen, underarms, groin and legs, sometimes alongside skin care.

name: Brazilian / intimate waxing
summary: Wax removal of pubic hair, from a swimsuit-line trim to full removal; common and well documented, with ingrown hairs and folliculitis as the usual complaints.
lead: Brazilian waxing, also called intimate or bikini waxing, is the removal of pubic hair using hot or cold wax pulled off with cloth strips or, in stripless forms, peeled off once hardened. Styles range from the American, which removes only the hair a swimsuit would show, through the French, which leaves a vertical strip, to the Brazilian or 'Hollywood', which removes all or nearly all hair.

name: Turmeric / gram flour hair removal paste
summary: A traditional South Asian herbal paste (ubtan-style) said to loosen or slow body hair; studied as a skin-care formulation, not as hair removal.
lead: Turmeric and gram flour pastes are folk preparations associated with ubtan, a traditional herbal skin-care formulation used in India and the surrounding region for a long time and now also sold as commercial products under the same name. Home versions are described by practitioners as a way to remove fine body hair or slow its regrowth.

name: Papaya enzyme hair inhibitor
summary: Folk idea that papaya's papain enzyme slows hair regrowth; the enzyme is real, the hair claim has no published trials behind it.
lead: Papain, also called papaya proteinase I, is a cysteine protease enzyme found in papaya (Carica papaya). It has commercial uses in leather, cosmetics, textiles, detergents, food and pharmaceuticals, is the active ingredient in many meat tenderisers, and appears in enzymatic wound-debriding products.

name: Sugar scrub / pumice exfoliation
summary: Abrasive scrubs and pumice stones that physically rub off dead skin; ancient and cheap, but dermatologists say it is not medically necessary.
lead: Mechanical exfoliation removes dead skin by physically scrubbing with an abrasive material. Tools include microfibre cloths, microbead scrubs, crushed nut shells, sugar or salt, pumice, sponges, loofahs and brushes. Pumice is a lightweight porous volcanic rock used as a mild abrasive for dead skin and unwanted hair.

name: Hair removal via topical hair-removal sprays
summary: Aerosol or spray depilatories that chemically dissolve hair at the skin surface; quick and painless, but results last only hours to days.
lead: Topical hair-removal sprays are aerosol or pump-applied chemical depilatories. Depilatories as a class come as gels, creams, lotions, aerosols, roll-ons and powders, and brands include Nair, Magic Shave and Veet.

name: Don't shave: hair-growth encouragement for body
summary: Letting chest and body hair grow out untrimmed to maximise its look; the 'shaving thickens hair' reasoning is not supported by the sources that address it, and hair density is mostly an androgen and genetics matter.
lead: 'Don't shave' is a practice in the chest-hair-maxxing corner of looksmaxxing culture: leaving chest, torso and limb hair untrimmed so that it reaches its natural density and length. Proponents treat body hair as a secondary sexual characteristic and want it to be as visible as possible.
claims: Shaving makes body hair grow back thicker and patchier, so stopping lets it fill in
Chest hair density is largely determined by androgens and genetics, not grooming
Body hair is a masculine signal worth growing out

name: Minoxidil for chest hair
summary: Off-label use of topical minoxidil to thicken chest hair; one registered trial exists but the sources give no published results, so appearance evidence is unproven.
lead: Minoxidil for chest hair is the off-label application of topical minoxidil, a drug approved for pattern hair loss on the scalp, to the chest in order to increase hair density or length. It appears in appearance forums as part of 'chest hair maxxing'.
claims: Topical minoxidil on the chest thickens chest hair

name: Hairy chest transplant / body hair transplant
summary: Surgical transfer of follicles by FUE; published work concerns moving body hair to the scalp, and cosmetic chest-hair transplants are barely studied.
lead: Body hair transplantation (BHT) is a form of follicular unit extraction (FUE) in which follicles are harvested from body regions such as the beard, chest or limbs . The published literature mostly concerns using body hair as additional donor supply for balding scalps, and uses in scars, cicatricial alopecia and vitiligo .

name: Laser for ingrown (pseudofolliculitis barbae)
summary: Laser hair reduction, often long-pulsed Nd:YAG, used to treat razor bumps (PFB) in people with curly beard hair; studied in small trials with favourable reported results.
lead: Pseudofolliculitis barbae (PFB), commonly 'razor bumps' or 'ingrowns', is an inflammatory condition in which shaved, curved hairs re-enter the skin and cause papules, pustules and sometimes pigmentation or scarring . It is most common in men with tightly curled beard hair and is associated with a keratin gene variant (K6hf A12T) .

name: Ilizarov external fixator lengthening
summary: The classic ring-fixator method of bone lengthening by distraction osteogenesis; well established in orthopaedics, with a documented high rate of problems and a long frame-wearing period.
lead: The Ilizarov apparatus is a circular external fixator, built from stainless steel or titanium rings attached to bone by wires and pins and linked by threaded rods . Developed by Gavriil Ilizarov in Kurgan, it is used for lengthening, deformity correction, non-union, bone transport and complex fractures . The Taylor Spatial Frame is a later development .
